Accusing an individual of altering the shutter of an irrigation tank for releasing more water to the ranches owned by a particular group of farmers, a group of villagers submitted petition to District Collector Anand Mohan on Monday.

A group of villagers from Gopalasamudram, who submitted the petition to the Collector during the weekly grievances redressal meeting held at the Collectorate on Monday, said the farmers of Gopalasamudram are getting water from Vaagaikulam, an irrigation tank in the village, for their agricultural operations for the past several decades.

Even as the water available in this systemised water body is being amicably shared by farmers from all sections of the society, an individual from Gopalasamudram Vadakkoor, who is the custodian of the shutter’s key, illegally altered the shutter of Vaagaikulam recently with an earthmover so as to ensure surplus supply of water to the lands belonging to a particular group of farmers.

When the affected farmers objected to this unlawful act, the problematic individual, is threatening others and repeatedly releasing videos that spread false information and foster enmity between to two different caste groups, the petitioners charged.

“These videos being shared on social media platforms portray the farmers belonging to a particular caste as anti-socials destroying Vaagaikulam and drive wedges between two caste groups. He claims that he had been empowered to decide on the quantum of water to be released from Vaagaikulam. The Collector should also take corrective measures to ensure equal distribution of water once again and take control of the operation of the shutter of Vaagaikulam,” the petitioners said.

Another group of villagers from Mela Kooniyoor near Cheranmahadevi submitted a petition seeking the eviction of “illegally built encroachments” on the Amman Temple Street being used by the public for decades. They said petitions were submitted with the officials against six individuals started constructing buildings on the “common path” being used by the villagers for several decades.

After petitions were submitted even with Sub-Collector, Cheranmahadevi, in July 2024, the ‘encroachers’ were asked to remove the illegal structures based on the inquiry conducted in December 2024. However, the Tahsildar of Cheranmahadevi, who had to conduct the encroachment eviction drive, refused to do so saying that he could act only on the direction from the “competent court”.

“Even though the Court has directed the revenue officials to evict the encroachments standing on the common path, this order is yet to be translated into action. Hence, the Collector should instruct his subordinates to remove the encroachments on the common path,” the petitioners said.
